findings.title: 2009 flexbox display values break the layouts that call these mixins
findings.body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit the 2009 box model (`display: -webkit-box`, `display: -moz-box`, `display: -webkit-inline-box`, `display: -moz-inline-box`) ahead of the 2012/modern values, and they never emit `display: -moz-flex` or `display: -moz-inline-flex`. Engines that only understand the 2009 keywords (Android 4.x stock browser, old iOS) will take that `display` and ignore the later ones. In that model `margin-left: auto` does not absorb free space, modern `align-items`/`order` do not apply, and `float` on the children is suppressed — so there is no float fallback either. That is exactly what the new call sites need: `.d-header .panel` was switched from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto`, and `.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously fell back to the parent `inline-block` when unprefixed `inline-flex` was ignored. Those browsers now drop the header controls (login, search, notifications) off the right edge and lay bullet badges out with the old box model. Firefox 22–27, which only had `-moz-flex`, gets no flex layout at all. Drop the 2009 `display: box` values; they are not a compatible prefix for the properties these call sites use.

findings.title: order() mixin writes a 0-based value into 1-based ordinal-group
findings.body: `@mixin order` assigns the same integer to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` as to `order` / `-webkit-order` / `-ms-flex-order`. The 2009 ordinal-group property is 1-based (initial value 1); `order` is 0-based (initial value 0). The legacy declarations must be `$val + 1`. As written, `@include order(1)` lands in the same group as items that set no order, so it will not sort after them the way `order: 1` does in modern browsers, and `order(0)` is an invalid ordinal-group. Header layout now depends on this mixin (`.panel` uses `order(3)`, `.extra-info-wrapper` uses `order(2)`). Those two values still sort after the default group by accident, but any `order(0)` or `order(1)` — including a plugin rule — will produce a different visual order in old WebKit than in current browsers and scramble the docked header.

findings.title: Header panel is no longer right-aligned without modern flexbox
findings.body: `.d-header .panel` lost `float: right` and `.d-header .title` lost `float: left`. The replacement is `margin-left: auto` and `order(3)` on the panel, which only pins the controls to the trailing edge when `.contents` is a modern flex container. If `display: flex` (and the 2012 prefixes) are ignored, `.panel` and `.title` are ordinary blocks: auto margins on a width:auto block compute to 0, so the logo and the header controls stack and the controls sit on the left. If the new mixin’s `display: -webkit-box` is what the engine honors, auto margins still do not pack to the end, and the removed floats cannot fall back because that display suppresses float. Login, search, and notification icons are the primary header controls. Keep `float: right` / `float: left` as the non-flex fallback, and do not activate a 2009 box display that disables it.

findings.title: Docked topic title can push header controls off-screen
findings.body: `.extra-info-wrapper` is now a flex item of `.d-header .contents` (`order: 2`, with `.panel` at `order: 3` and `margin-left: auto` so topic info sits between the logo and the controls). Nothing in the new rules sets `min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden`, or a flex basis on `.extra-info-wrapper` or `.title`, and `.contents` does not set `flex-wrap` (so it stays `nowrap`). Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, which will not shrink below the content’s minimum size. A long docked topic title therefore widens the flex line past the viewport instead of ellipsizing, and `margin-left: auto` cannot pull `.panel` back in — the user menu and notifications are pushed off-screen. Set `min-width: 0` (and overflow/ellipsis on the title child) on `.extra-info-wrapper`.

findings.title: Small-action row no longer spans the stream or pins its button
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex row, but the action control is still `button { float: right }` (line 309) and `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%` with no `flex: 1` / `min-width: 0`. Float is ignored on flex items, and a float inside a flex item is positioned against that item’s content box, not the full row. The description (or a wrapping `.topic-body`) shrinks to its content, so expand/undo/remove buttons sit beside the text instead of at the right edge of the topic stream. In browsers that do not apply flex, `.topic-avatar` is still `float: left` (line 270) but the 4em padding that cleared that float is gone, so the description overlaps the icon. Vertical spacing was also removed (`margin-top: 5px`, `padding-top: 4px`, and custom-message `margin: 5px 0`), so multi-line custom messages are flush with the row edges. Give the text column `flex: 1` and `min-width: 0`, pin the button with `margin-left: auto` if it is a flex item, and keep a non-flex padding fallback so the text does not cover the avatar.
